name: waiver: a quote kept exactly as written
description: A returning agent writes a short product post that must quote a teammate word for word as a block quote, em dash included. It should keep the quote, waive only the rule it breaks with a reason above the block, keep the waiver in the shipped file, fix every other finding instead of waiving it, and run inkling waivers with the reader test before it ships.
answer: Platform engineers who tried to self-host before and gave up, or who are evaluating us. I want them to try the install again. Quote Priya exactly, as a block quote. About 15 minutes.
criteria: The waiver's reason says why the break is the point of the line (the quote is kept as the person wrote it), not taste (waivers: "The judge accepts a reason that shows the break is the point of the line ... It rejects taste (\"sounds better\", \"style\", \"it's shorter\")").

Every other rule finding was fixed in the text rather than waived; any other waiver in the final piece has a reason a fresh judge would accept, and none was left after `inkling waivers` rejected it (README: "Breaking an Inkling rule is allowed only with a strong reason, written into the draft as a waiver and checked by a judge that never saw the writer").

The agent ran `inkling waivers` with `--readers` pointing at a reader test run, so a reader had to quote the line working (waivers: "Run `inkling waivers <file> --readers <run dir>` before you ship"; "With `--readers`, the waiver also needs a reader in that test who quoted the line working").
The agent stopped once the core expectations passed and the waiver counted, and its last message says what is still open, if anything (step 9: "Stop editing when the core expectations pass").
The piece names no company or product the request didn't name, and runs no house the request didn't ask for (houses: "Use a house only when the request says the piece is for that company").
